claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr forms a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The WTaTiVZr solid solution has severe lattice distortion and local chemical complexity.
Lattice distortion and local chemical complexity increase resistance to dislocation slip in WTaTiVZr.
Increased dislocation-slip resistance in WTaTiVZr promotes crack-tip plasticity relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed BCC solid-solution state gives WTaTiVZr greater elevated-temperature plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten is limited by intrinsic brittleness and a lack of solid-solution strengthening.
The comparison uses fully recrystallized, polycrystalline WTaTiVZr and commercially pure tungsten with comparable grain sizes.
Both materials will be subjected to identical tensile or fracture-toughness testing at 800–1200°C in vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
The mechanical comparison excludes irradiation and corrosive environments.
Pure tungsten has a comparatively undistorted BCC lattice.
Lattice distortion and chemical complexity raise the critical resolved shear stress in WTaTiVZr.
The proposed mechanism distributes crack-tip plasticity and delays crack initiation and propagation.
Pure tungsten remains prone to brittle fracture over the specified high-temperature range.
WTaTiVZr will have higher plastic strain to failure than pure tungsten under the specified conditions.
WTaTiVZr will have higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten under the specified conditions.
The hypothesis is restricted to equimolar WTaTiVZr that remains single-phase BCC at 800–1200°C without irradiation or corrosive attack.
Alloy decomposition or intermetallic formation may alter the predicted behavior.
The magnitude of any improvement is unknown because direct plastic-strain and toughness data are lacking.
